resources.string: When safe mode is on, no plugins are loaded. Use it if a plugin breaks the app.
No plugins installed. Tap Install from file to add a .py or .plugin file.
Plugin %1$s was disabled after a crash.
Delete plugin %1$s? This cannot be undone.
%1$s has not returned control for several seconds and is freezing the app. Disable it and restart?
This file could not be recognised as a plugin, so there is no telling what it does. Installed anyway, it gets everything: your messages, your files, the network and the app\'s own code.
The plugin engine is off. Turn it on in Settings → Plugins first.
Prevents plugin hook failures by disabling ART Profile Saver.
The SDK is bundled with the app, so there is nothing to download or update.
This plugin asks for nothing beyond its own menu items and settings screen.
Its own menu items, dialogs and settings screen are always allowed and are not asked about.
The plugin also declares: %1$s. There is no switch for that yet: the app cannot actually stop it, and a switch that changes nothing would only mislead you.
Rewriting the app\'s code puts this plugin above everything else on this list — with it, the plugin can read and send your messages even with those switches off. Keep it only for authors you trust.
Plugin restarted, the change is in effect.
This plugin is no longer installed.
Add its own menus and settings
Menu items, dialogs and a settings screen of its own.
Sees your chat list and the text of messages as they arrive, private ones included.
Send, edit and delete messages as you
Whatever it sends looks like it came from you, and it can change or delete what you wrote.
Reach the internet on its own
Can contact any server, including sending there whatever it has read.
Reach files outside its own folder
Can open your downloads and save or overwrite files anywhere the app can reach.
Handle the links and files you open
Sees the links you tap and the files you open, and can take them over instead of the app.
Can turn the app\'s own options on and off without asking you.
Change how the app itself works
Xposed hooks: rewrites the app\'s code while it runs. Everything else on this list becomes possible for it anyway.
It asks for nothing beyond its own menu items and settings screen.
A manifest is a promise. This is the record of what the plugin reached for while it ran, and what was refused.
Asked for something it never uses? Revoke it — nothing breaks. Reaching for something it never asked for is worth a closer look.
The record lives in memory and is lost when the app restarts.
Its own menus, dialogs and settings screen. Nothing else — no messages, no files, no network.
You hand out permissions one by one, and the app enforces them.
Lets you grant Xposed hooks — rewriting the app\'s code as it runs. Nothing below can be enforced against a plugin that has them.
New plugins start here. Raise the level only for what you actually need — a plugin that never gets the level never gets the reach.
Permissions below are yours to give and take back. Rewriting the app\'s code needs the Trusted level.
At this level the switches below are courtesy, not enforcement: a plugin that rewrites the app\'s code can undo any of them. Keep it only for authors you trust.
It will be installed **isolated**: its own menus and settings screen, nothing more. You decide what else it gets, on the plugin\'s screen.
It does not say what it needs. Isolated it stays harmless; give it anything only if you trust the author.
It asks for Xposed hooks — rewriting the app\'s code while it runs. That is not a permission among others — granting it puts the plugin above every other switch. Only the Trusted level allows it.
This plugin never said what it needs, so everything it could possibly ask for is listed above.
Tried to read another module\'s state
This level only unlocks the last switch — Xposed hooks. While it stays off, everything above is enforced as usual.
